text.p: Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu Oy said on Monday its outlook had improved but earnings in the early part of 1997 were likely to remain modest.
"The Outokumpu group's outlook for 1997 has improved during the past few months although a great deal of uncertainty prevails," Outokumpu said in a statement with its 1997 results.

"Market conditions are forecast to improve during 1997. The strength of the U.S. dollar will also improve conditions for profitability. Earnings in the early part of the year are nevertheless likely to remain modest," it said.
Outokumpu earlier said its profit before extraordinary items and tax fell in 1996 to 229 million from 1.48 billion in 1995.
